tn_jenga_area.blurb: A cluster of big boulders beside the Laurel Falls trail in Laurel Snow State Natural Area near Dayton, reached after a long uphill walk from the trailhead and then only a few minutes past the trail split. A dozen bouldering problems are recorded, and none are beginner-level: most sit from V4 up, with several in the V8 to V11 range, so this is a spot for people who already boulder hard. The line the area is named for is a very hard single-move problem, and the trail itself runs through a cave beneath one of the blocks. Problems are short, so bring several pads.

tn_solstice_cave.blurb: A steep, overhanging cave on the South Clear Creek side of the Obed, entered by a ledge traverse with a fixed cable along the cliff. Twelve routes are recorded, mostly sport with a few trad lines. Grades start around 5.6, but the cave is really about hard roof climbing: a handful of 5.9s and a 5.10 and 5.11 give way to three 5.12s and three 5.13s. Expect powerful moves on big overhanging terrain, and bring a stick clip and extra quickdraws. South Clear Creek is a busy part of the Obed, and winter is the comfortable season because the area gets very hot in summer.

tn_h_cbd_wall.blurb: One of the walls at Woodcock Cove, a long sandstone cliffline near Dunlap in Sequatchie County, roughly an hour from Chattanooga. The trail ends at two steel ladders bolted to the rock, which lead down to the base. The wall holds eleven routes, eight sport and three trad, and the difficulty is friendly: everything falls between 5.7 and 5.10, with five climbs at 5.10. It sits across from a freestanding pillar, and makes a good stop for climbers who want moderate single-pitch routes.

tn_area_x.blurb: The cliff farthest down the Obed River, reached on a faint side trail that leaves the walk to Tyranny. It is secluded and quiet, and the routes are usually in shade, so it works well in hot weather. Eleven climbs are recorded, eight sport and three trad, ranging from about 5.8 into the low 5.12s, with the best concentration in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. The rock is the hard, horizontally layered kind found throughout the Obed. The first few routes sit apart from the main cliff, past the two trad cracks.

tn_hidden_secret.blurb: A small group of boulders in the woods above another block at the Boulders on Old Wauhatchie Pike, a city bouldering park in Chattanooga. Eleven problems are recorded, and the grades are gentle: most are V0 to V3, with one standout near V6. The mix is described as faces, mantles and an interesting traverse, so it suits beginners and anyone warming up. The walk in from the main part of the park is only a few minutes.

tn_inner_circle_the.blurb: A steep sport wall in the North Clear Creek section of the Obed, with one of the shortest walks in the area. The routes run up very steep rock, and tree cover keeps the base partly shaded until midday even though the wall faces south. Eleven routes are recorded, almost all sport, and the difficulty is serious: a couple of 5.10s, five at 5.11 and four at 5.12. A stick clip is a smart thing to carry. It suits climbers who already lead in the 5.11 range.

tn_high_water_wall.blurb: A wall at King's Bluff, the limestone crag above the Cumberland River in Clarksville, around 45 minutes from Nashville. The approach is a short stair descent, then left to a spot just before The Beach. Eleven routes are recorded, nine sport and two trad, with a spread of 5.9s, a couple of 5.10s, four at 5.11 and one 5.12. Routes get less traffic than the busier walls nearby, though the base is close enough to the river that a flood can reach it. Climbs at the bluff are mostly 45 to 55 feet.

tn_p_the_still_house.blurb: A less developed, quieter corner of Woodcock Cove, the sandstone cliffline near Dunlap in Sequatchie County. Eleven routes are recorded, seven sport and four trad, spanning easy 5.6 terrain up to 5.13, with most between 5.8 and 5.12. It sees fewer climbers than the neighbouring wall along the main trail. The way down is a short scramble helped by a fixed rope, then you continue along the base of the cliff. It suits a mixed party that wants a few moderates and some hard sport lines in one place.

_conflicts.tn_solstice_cave: Stored rock is conglomerate; the Obed parent page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105891970/obed-clear-creek) calls the Obed rock Cumberland Plateau sandstone. Not changed; blurb names no rock.
